revision_notes: Fetched and re-verified the DLA Piper Tanzania pages (last modified 24 March 2026). The Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (in force 1 May 2023) restricts transfer of personal data outside Tanzania broadly: transfers are permitted only to states with adequate protection or under specified safeguards, and the data controller/processor must obtain a PDPC permit before transfer, evidenced by an international/bilateral agreement or contractual safeguards. This is a comprehensive, cross-sector requirement consistent with code 4. Searched for evidence of stricter, enforced, multi-sector data storage mandates (e.g. payment or telecoms data required to be stored domestically) but found no explicit in-country storage requirement beyond the PDPA's transfer-permit regime, so did not promote to the top code (5). Score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act 2022, in force since 1 May 2023, imposes comprehensive restrictions on the transfer of personal data outside the country. Transfers are permitted only to states offering adequate protection or under specified safeguards, and data controllers and processors must obtain a permit from the Personal Data Protection Commission before transferring personal data abroad, supported by proof of an international or bilateral data protection agreement or contractual safeguards with the overseas recipient. These requirements apply broadly across personal data categories rather than being confined to a single sector.

Definition: Whether the country has enacted comprehensive data protection and privacy legislation. A foundational legal requirement for building trust in digital public infrastructure and for enabling secure cross-border data flows under frameworks like the AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection.
Value Name: Legislation enacted with Data Protection Authority established
revision_notes: Fetched and re-verified the DLA Piper Tanzania page, confirming the Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (in force 1 May 2023, Chapter 44) establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission (PDPC) as supervisory authority, consistent with code 4. Further searches found evidence of active enforcement: the PDPC awarded monetary compensation for a privacy violation in Abdul Said Naumanga v Mi Casa Company Limited (2025), the High Court largely upheld the PDPA in Tito Elias Magoti and Another v The Attorney General (2024), and the Minister of Communication and ICT issued a nationwide compliance-registration ultimatum backed by threatened legal action in January 2026. This points towards a maturing, actively-enforced regime (potentially code 5), but Tanzania has signed, not ratified, the AU Malabo Convention, so the 'regional alignment' element of the top code is not clearly satisfied. Given this ambiguity, the score is confirmed at 4 rather than promoted, and the row is flagged for human review in case reviewers judge the evidence sufficient for the top code.
revised_comments: Tanzania's Personal Data Protection Act 2022 (Chapter 44), in force since 1 May 2023, establishes the Personal Data Protection Commission as the independent supervisory authority responsible for registration of data controllers and processors, investigation of complaints, and enforcement, including administrative fines and compensation orders. The Commission has begun active enforcement of the Act, including a 2025 ruling awarding monetary compensation for a privacy violation and a January 2026 nationwide compliance-registration drive for public and private institutions handling personal data, backed by the threat of legal action once the grace period expires.
